chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman ibn Ayyub al-Khazzaz said: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi said: I said to Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him):
"For what reason did Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, place the souls in the bodies after they had been in His highest realm in the loftiest place?"

He (peace be upon him) replied: "Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, knew that whenever the souls were left in their state of honor and elevation, most of them would incline towards claiming lordship for themselves other than Him, the Mighty and High,
so He placed them by His Power into the bodies which He had decreed for them from the beginning of the Divine Decree, observing them and having mercy upon them,
and made some of them in need of others, and attached some to others, and elevated some above others in degrees, and sufficed some by others,

and sent to them His messengers and appointed for them His proofs, bearers of good news and warners, commanding them to engage in servitude and humility to their Lord through the types of acts that make them servants,

and established for them punishments in the immediate world and punishments in the Hereafter, and rewards in the immediate world and rewards in the Hereafter, to make them desire good through that and to make them disdain evil,
and to humble them through seeking sustenance and earnings, so that they may know thereby that they are servants and created beings,
and devote themselves to His worship, so that they may deserve thereby the eternal bliss and the Garden of Eternity,
and be safe from inclining to what is not rightfully theirs.
Then he (peace be upon him) said: "O son of al-Fadl! Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has a better view for His servants than they have for themselves,
do you not see that you see in them nothing but a love for elevation over others,
so that among them is one who has inclined towards claiming lordship, and among them is one who has inclined towards claiming prophethood without its right,
and among them is one who has inclined towards claiming Imamate without its right,
despite what they see in themselves of deficiency, inability, weakness, lowliness, need, poverty, alternating pains, and the overpowering death that subdues them all.
O son of al-Fadl! Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, does nothing for His servants except what is best for them, and He does not oppress people at all, but people oppress themselves.
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah place souls in physical bodies according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the wisdom behind the descent of souls into bodies, emphasizing that physical limitations and needs serve as a divine mercy to curb the soul's innate tendency toward arrogance and self-deification. This theological perspective underscores the Shia concept of *al-Aslah* (what is best for the servant), illustrating how material constraints facilitate spiritual humility and the recognition of *ubudiyyah* (servitude), thereby ensuring the soul's ultimate worthiness for eternal bliss.
